reconstructed_theorem_text:
Objects: For n in N put t[n,i]=i*T/2^n for i=0,...,2^n, and Delta_i^n Z=Z(t[n,i+1])-Z(t[n,i]). Define Z_n,i=(B(t[n,i+1],omega)-B(t[n,i],omega))^2-(t[n,i+1]-t[n,i]); the latter difference is subtraction in R_+ before casting to R, equal to T/2^n on this grid.

Domains: Omega with measurable space m; mu a measure; B:R_+ x Omega->R; filtration on R_+; T>=0; weights a_n,i:Omega->R for n in N, 0<=i<2^n; C real. No finite-measure instance is stated.

Quantifiers: Universally Omega,m,mu,B,filtration,hB,T,weight,hAdapted,hWeight,C,hC; weight hypotheses are for every level n and index i; then n->infinity.

Assumptions: For each finite family of times, the corresponding B-values have the centered joint Gaussian law with covariance Cov(B_s,B_t)=min(s,t). The paths of B are mu-a.e. continuous; in particular B_0=0 almost surely, with no pointwise initial-value requirement. B is strongly adapted, and every increment B_t-B_s, s<=t, is independent of filtration(s). Each a_n,i is strongly measurable with respect to filtration(t[n,i]) at the left grid endpoint, and is in L^2(mu). The bound integral a_n,i^2 dmu<=C holds uniformly for all n,i.

Conclusion: The real sequence integral_Omega (sum_{i=0}^{2^n-1} a_n,i(omega)*Z_n,i(omega))^2 dmu tends to zero.

Scopes: Only convergence of the displayed real integral values is explicitly concluded, without a separate full-sum integrability assertion. T may be zero. Neither usual conditions nor a finite-mu instance are separately hypothesized.

Constant dependencies: C is given and uniform over levels and cells; it may depend on all preceding chosen data. No rate is specified.
